title: Authorizing Official risk acceptance expectations
notes: Pinned excerpts for AO review Q&A generation and grading. Graders must use retrieved section text plus the student's compiled authorization package — not parametric knowledge of RMF practice.

sections.title: Authorizing Official role
sections.text: The Authorizing Official (AO) is accountable for accepting residual risk to organizational operations, assets, individuals, and other organizations. An authorization decision is based on the complete authorization package — typically including the system security plan (SSP), assessment results or findings, and the plan of action and milestones (POA&M). The AO expects clear linkage between implemented controls, known weaknesses, planned remediation, and residual risk that will remain after planned actions.

sections.title: Risk acceptance criteria
sections.text: Risk acceptance is an explicit decision that residual risk is within organizational tolerance for a defined period or condition. Strong justifications identify the weakness or control gap, the residual likelihood and impact after compensating controls, who is accountable, and what monitoring or revisit triggers apply. Weak justifications merely assert that risk is 'low' or 'acceptable' without tying the claim to evidence in the SSP, assessment findings, or POA&M.

sections.title: POA&M items and acceptance decisions
sections.text: POA&M entries with status risk_accepted, delayed, or long-dated completion require AO-facing rationale. The AO will ask whether remediation timelines are realistic, whether compensating controls reduce residual risk enough to continue operation, and whether open weaknesses undermine claims in the SSP control implementation narratives. Acceptance should not be used to hide unfinished remediation without a clear residual-risk story.

sections.title: SSP implementation traceability
sections.text: SSP control implementation statements should be consistent with known findings and POA&M items. If a control is described as implemented while related weaknesses remain open, the AO expects an explanation of scope boundaries, compensating controls, or planned closure. Responsible roles named in the SSP should be able to own remediation or acceptance decisions for associated gaps.

sections.title: Machine-readable package integrity
sections.text: When OSCAL (or other machine-readable) artifacts accompany the package, the AO expects them to reflect the same system boundary, control posture, and open items described in narrative SSP and POA&M content. Contradictions between generated OSCAL artifacts and the student's written SSP/POA&M undermine confidence in the authorization package and should be explained or corrected before acceptance.

sections.title: Conditions and continuous monitoring
sections.text: Authorization and risk acceptance are often conditional. The AO looks for monitoring measures, revisit dates, or event-driven triggers (for example, missed POA&M dates, control degradation, or significant system change) that would reopen the residual-risk decision. Packages that accept risk without any monitoring or revisit condition leave the organization blind to growing exposure.
